title: Allocation Classifier
description: In MicroPython, a statement allocates heap memory when it creates a new object that is not a small integer. Small integers (from -2**30 to 2**30 - 1 on the Pico's 32-bit port) live inside the value itself, and storing into an existing buffer never allocates. Everything else (floats, slices, lists, tuples, strings, big integers) creates garbage that the collector must clean up later.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: What do all the statements that do not allocate have in common?
A memoryview slice copies no data. Why does it still allocate?
Why would statement 11 give a different answer on a 64-bit computer?
commonMisconceptions: (1) Any arithmetic is free. (2) A slice never copies. (3) Floats are stored inside the value, like small integers. (4) Writing into an array allocates.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all twelve statements. Mastery is 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt.
